purpose: Map the observables required by the frozen dual-mode literature taxonomy to quantities that the current quasi-one-dimensional project solver can or cannot support. This record does not assign LBW/YBW labels and does not invent a precombustion shock-train detector.

valid_uses: combustor-entry Mach when the domain coordinate and entry station are source-backed
native_solver_observables.forbidden_inference: A minimum Mach below one anywhere in the domain is not by itself a ram/dual-mode label.

valid_uses: source-specific station pressure if coordinate and normalization are source-backed
native_solver_observables.forbidden_inference: A generic pressure-rise threshold is not a universal shock-train or mode detector.
Temperature alone does not identify ram/scram mode.
Geometry alone does not define the combustion mode.

native_solver_observables.quantity: prescribed energy/momentum/fuel source profiles where a study supplies them
native_solver_observables.forbidden_inference: A prescribed heat input is not automatically an experimentally measured heat-release distribution or a mode label.
Numerical nonconvergence is not physical inlet unstart unless an independent source-backed unstart criterion is satisfied.

not_natively_resolved.reason: The production model has no dedicated strength-adaptable isolator/precombustion-shock model equivalent to Tian et al.'s X-shock treatment and no frozen shock-train detector.
No source-backed detector maps the current first-order quasi-1D pressure/Mach solution to a physical shock-train length, and multidimensional separation is not represented.
The current quasi-one-dimensional model does not resolve multidimensional shock/boundary-layer separation topology.
No finite-rate chemistry/flame-front or optical diagnostic is solved.
The present solver does not transport H2/H2O or other reacting species.

domain_specific_findings.reason: The accepted reduced domain starts at the hydrogen-injection station and was constructed as a scoped heated-flow reference benchmark, not an isolator + combustor mode-transition model. It cannot observe an upstream precombustion shock train.
The accepted case is non-reactive/source-free. Its isolator-length result was explicitly found inert in the inviscid cold-flow model and cannot establish reactive combustion mode.

A future mode-transition case must include a source-backed isolator/combustor coordinate mapping and an admissible representation or detector for the precombustion shock state before literature mode labels can be assigned.

classification_policy.reason: The project's current accepted study cases do not jointly expose the literature's central isolator/precombustion-shock observable, and the literal LBW/YBW project labels remain undefined.
next_evidence_needed: Explicit project/teacher definition of LBW and YBW.
Source-backed future mode-transition geometry/domain containing the relevant isolator and combustor-entry station.
Source-backed method for representing or detecting the precombustion shock state in the reduced-order model, or an alternative authoritative criterion that is observable with the current solver.
Decision on steady/quasi-steady versus hysteretic transition-map scope.
